docs.title: MicroTrace Documentation
docs.text:
MicroTrace is a firmware analysis platform that combines:

  • an Electron desktop app
  • a TypeScript frontend
  • a FastAPI backend for projects and analysis
  • an MCP-powered AI workspace
  • Elasticsearch-backed register lookup
  • optional Docker deployment for the whole stack

docs.title: What This Documentation Covers
docs.text:
This documentation set is split into two main audiences:

  • Users Users who want to configure Ghidra, analyze firmware, inspect results, and work with the MCP assistant.
  • Developers Contributors who need to understand architecture, APIs, runtime behavior, Docker deployment, and documentation workflow.

docs.title: How To Use Git Submodules
docs.text:
This project keeps the documentation site as a separate repository inside the main codebase by using a git submodule.

Current submodule example in MicroTrace:

docs-site/ -> https://github.com/omarsawaf1/MicroTrace-Docs.git

docs.title: Why Use a Submodule
docs.text:
Submodules are useful when:

  • you want separate git history
  • you want a repo to live inside another repo
  • you do not want to copy documentation files into the main project

docs.title: Clone a Repository With Submodules
docs.text: git clone --recurse-submodules <repo-url>

docs.title: Initialize Submodules After a Normal Clone
docs.text: git submodule update --init --recursive

docs.title: Pull the Latest Docs Changes
docs.text: git submodule update --remote --merge docs-site

docs.title: Edit the Submodule
docs.text:
1. Enter the submodule directory:
cd docs-site
  1. Create or edit files as normal
  2. Commit inside the submodule
  3. Return to the main repository
  4. Commit the updated submodule pointer in the main repository

docs.title: Common Workflow
docs.text:
cd docs-site
git checkout main
git pull

Make documentation changes, then:

git add .
git commit -m "Update docs"
git push

Then in the parent repository:

cd ..
git add docs-site
git commit -m "Update docs-site submodule pointer"

docs.title: Important Rule
docs.text:
Warning

A submodule is not stored as a normal folder in the parent repository. The parent repository stores a pointer to a specific commit of the child repository.

docs.title: Submodule looks empty
docs.text:
Run:

git submodule update --init --recursive

docs.title: Submodule is on detached HEAD
docs.text:
Inside the submodule:

git checkout main

Then pull or commit normally.

docs.title: Documentation Overview
docs.text: This section contains the full product documentation for MicroTrace.

docs.title: Product Summary
docs.text: MicroTrace helps users reverse engineer embedded firmware by combining static analysis, project management, graph visualization, register search, and an AI-assisted MCP workflow.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Upload firmware projects and manage analysis runs
  • Execute Ghidra headless analysis and store artifacts
  • Parse decompiled code and assembly listings into graph-friendly structures
  • Search register and peripheral data through Elasticsearch
  • Use an MCP-based assistant for register extraction, PDF tooling, and guided analysis
  • Run locally in Electron or as a containerized web stack

docs.title: High-Level Design
docs.text:
MicroTrace is split into independently understandable layers:

  • UI layer Vite-rendered frontend pages plus Electron shell logic
  • Backend layer FastAPI service for projects, settings, graph data, and analysis
  • MCP layer FastAPI wrapper plus MCP tool server and LLM orchestration
  • Persistence layer JSON project state, analysis artifacts, and Elasticsearch-backed register search

The backend coordinates:

docs.text: Module Responsibility main.py app factory and service wiring api/routes/ FastAPI endpoints services/analysis_service.py orchestrates analysis services/ghidra_service.py launches Ghidra headless services/result_store.py stores artifacts services/register_lookup_service.py Elasticsearch-backed register search repositories/ settings and project persistence

docs.title: Application Wiring
docs.text:
The backend uses a service container pattern assembled in create_app().

app = FastAPI(
    title="MicroTrace Firmware Backend",
    version="1.0.0",
    lifespan=lifespan,
)
app.state.services = services

docs.title: Project Analysis Flow
docs.text:
run = services.analysis_service.run_project_analysis(project_id)

That call:

  1. loads the project
  2. resolves the effective Ghidra path
  3. creates run artifacts
  4. calls Ghidra export
  5. parses outputs into graph-ready payloads
  6. stores and indexes run state

docs.title: Artifact Layout
docs.text:
Each analysis run creates:

  decompiled_code.txt
  listing.txt

docs.title: Deployment Goals
docs.text:
The Docker stack is designed to:

  • keep frontend, backend, MCP, and Elasticsearch isolated
  • expose one browser entrypoint
  • support host-mounted Ghidra
  • preserve runtime data in named volumes

docs.title: Compose Services
docs.text: Service Role frontend nginx-based web entrypoint and reverse proxy backend FastAPI application mcpserver MCP FastAPI service elasticsearch register search backend

docs.title: Reverse Proxy Behavior
docs.text:
location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://backend:8000/api/;
}

location /mcp/ {
    proxy_pass http://mcpserver:8001/;
}

docs.title: Volume Strategy
docs.text: Volume Purpose elasticsearch_data Elasticsearch data backend_state backend runtime state backend_output analysis outputs mcp_runtime MCP logs, settings, and conversations

docs.text:
• unprivileged nginx runtime
  • non-root Python containers
  • no-new-privileges:true
  • slim and Wolfi-based images where practical

docs.text:

  5. verify frontend can call /api and /mcp

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
MicroTrace uses Ghidra headless mode to export the raw analysis artifacts needed by the backend:

  • listing.txt
  • decompiled_code.txt
  • project-local analysis outputs

docs.title: Why Headless Mode Matters
docs.text:
Headless execution lets the platform:

  • automate analysis runs from the backend
  • avoid GUI-driven manual export
  • standardize output locations and arguments
  • run in desktop workflows and containerized environments

docs.title: Execution Pattern
docs.text:
The backend eventually delegates to the Ghidra launcher with arguments similar to:

analyzeHeadless <project_dir> <project_name> -import <firmware> -scriptPath <script_dir> -postScript export_disasm.py ...

docs.title: MicroTrace-Specific Role
docs.text:
The backend service:

  1. validates the configured Ghidra path
  2. creates a new analysis artifact directory
  3. calls Ghidra headless
  4. expects exported text artifacts
  5. parses those artifacts into graph data

docs.title: Runtime Relationship
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Backend --> Ghidra[analyzeHeadless]
    Ghidra --> ExportScript[export_disasm.py]
    ExportScript --> Listing[listing.txt]
    ExportScript --> Decompiled[decompiled_code.txt]
    Listing --> Parsers
    Decompiled --> Parsers

docs.title: Local and Electron mode
docs.text:
Users provide a real host path such as:

D:\Tools\ghidra\support\analyzeHeadless.bat

docs.title: Docker mode
docs.text:
The host Ghidra folder is mounted to /opt/ghidra, so the container path becomes:

/opt/ghidra/support/analyzeHeadless

docs.title: Ghidra path is configured but analysis fails
docs.text:
Check:

  • file exists
  • path is absolute
  • file name is analyzeHeadless or analyzeHeadless.bat

docs.title: Artifacts missing
docs.text:
Check:

  • export script exists
  • Ghidra returned success
  • output directory permissions are valid

docs.title: Important Behavior
docs.text:
In Docker mode:

  • the host path comes from .env
  • the container path becomes /opt/ghidra

The UI may still show the configured Ghidra value, but the actual host mount must exist before containers start.

docs.title: Common Local Issues
docs.text:
Missing Ghidra

If Ghidra is not configured, project creation still works, but analysis requests will fail.

MCP service offline

The MCP UI can load, but chat and tool actions will fail until the MCP FastAPI service is reachable.

docs.title: Runtime Modes
docs.text:
MicroTrace currently supports three practical ways to run:

  1. Local development Run the frontend, backend, and MCP services from source.
  2. Electron desktop Launch the packaged desktop shell that starts backend services for the user.
  3. Docker stack Run frontend, backend, MCP server, and Elasticsearch as containers.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
MicroTrace uses SVD-backed register information to enrich function analysis and support register search.

This data is ultimately used to:

  • map addresses and registers to peripherals
  • improve register search responses
  • enrich analysis nodes with hardware context

docs.title: What the Data Represents
docs.text:
Typical register records include:

  • peripheral name
  • peripheral base address
  • register name
  • register description
  • field names and bit positions
  • normalized address values

docs.title: Conceptual Model
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    SVD[SVD file] --> Parse[Parse peripheral/register/field metadata]
    PDF[Reference manual PDF] --> Base[Extract or confirm base addresses]
    Parse --> Merge[Normalize and merge metadata]
    Base --> Merge
    Merge --> Index[Searchable register dataset]
    Index --> Backend[Backend register lookup service]

docs.title: How It Helps the Product
docs.text:
The backend register lookup service can use this structured data to:

  • answer /api/v1/registers queries
  • enrich pointer references detected during analysis
  • give more meaningful peripheral context in UI displays

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text: GET /api/v1/registers?q=USART&size=20

docs.title: Typical Record Shape
docs.text:
{
  "PERIPHERAL": "FLASH",
  "BASEADDRESS": "0X40023C00",
  "REGISTER": "ACR",
  "FIELD": "LATENCY",
  "BITOFFSET": 0,
  "BITWIDTH": 3
}

docs.text: The old SVD database notes were retained conceptually because the topic is still useful, but they have been rewritten to fit the current MicroTrace architecture and backend usage.

docs.title: What the MCP Workspace Does
docs.text:
The MCP UI is the assistant-oriented workspace in MicroTrace. It provides:

  • chat sessions
  • provider switching between OpenAI, LM Studio, and Ollama
  • quick actions for PDF and register tooling
  • model configuration and persistence

docs.title: Quick Actions
docs.text:
The UI exposes common tool-assisted workflows:

  • extract registers from a datasheet PDF
  • search for a register
  • fetch a specific register with detail
  • extract images from a PDF
  • read PDF table of contents

docs.title: Supported Model Providers
docs.text: Provider Typical Base URL OpenAI https://api.openai.com/v1 LM Studio http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 Ollama http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1

docs.title: MCP Request Path
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant MCPUI
    participant MCPAPI
    participant MCPClient
    participant ToolServer
    participant LLM

    User->>MCPUI: Send question
    MCPUI->>MCPAPI: POST /query
    MCPAPI->>MCPClient: continue_query()
    MCPClient->>LLM: chat completion with tools
    LLM->>ToolServer: request tool call
    ToolServer-->>MCPClient: tool result
    MCPClient->>LLM: final completion
    MCPClient-->>MCPAPI: assistant message
    MCPAPI-->>MCPUI: response payload

docs.text:
{
  "provider": "ollama",
  "model": "llama3.1:8b",
  "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1",
  "api_key": ""
}

docs.title: Good Operational Advice
docs.text:
Tip

Use OpenAI when you want hosted models, LM Studio for local desktop inference, and Ollama when you want a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint with easy model management.

docs.title: Ghidra Path Validation Rules
docs.text:
The backend validates that the configured Ghidra executable:

  • is an absolute path
  • points to a file
  • has a valid name such as analyzeHeadless or analyzeHeadless.bat

docs.title: Analysis returns 409
docs.text:
Cause: - Ghidra path is not configured

Fix: - open settings and save the correct Ghidra executable path

docs.title: Analysis returns 422
docs.text:
Cause: - path exists in settings but is invalid

Fix: - reselect the executable - ensure it points to the actual Ghidra headless launcher

docs.title: Graph is empty
docs.text:
Cause: - analysis artifacts were not generated - parsing produced no functions

Fix: - inspect backend logs - inspect listing.txt and decompiled_code.txt

docs.title: MCP UI says API offline
docs.text:
Cause: - MCP FastAPI service is not running

Fix: - verify port 8001 - verify Electron or Docker started the MCP service

docs.title: Troubleshooting Checklist
docs.text:
• Can the backend health endpoint load?
  • Is Ghidra configured?
  • Was analysis.json written?
  • Is Elasticsearch reachable?
  • Is the MCP service healthy?
